integrity: The proof uses Kummer's theorem, an exhaustive classification of no-borrow subdigit selections for the two-digit row, and an explicit one-borrow witness. A standalone standard-library verifier checks structural, exhaustive-borrow, and direct integer-gcd cases. Closest primary literature was inspected and implication-compared; one supporting paper was available only through its abstract and a detailed source-level comparison in the closest recent paper.
limitations: The theorem treats rows with exactly two nonzero base-p digits, both equal to one. It overlaps known plus/minus-one cases and does not classify arbitrary rows or determine the full gcd. Absolute bibliographic novelty cannot be certified by search.
title: Sparse two-digit rows force a single p-adic factor in restricted binomial GCDs
